content:
Apple's September was already quite exciting, but they seem ready to continue that momentum in October, with what could be several long-awaited product launches.

#1: MacBook Pro / Ultra with a brand-new design featuring a touchscreen

The Mac has long refused to include a touchscreen, but that may finally be about to change — rumours suggest Apple will unveil a new MacBook Pro (or MacBook Ultra) in October.

Apple's next-generation MacBook Pro will feature an all-new industrial design, the first major overhaul in five years. Besides adding touch capability, it will also come with an OLED display, Dynamic Island, and may offer a C2 cellular modem option.

The MacBook Pro hasn't had a fresh look for a long time, and touchscreens have been around for even longer — yet Apple has consistently chosen not to add this feature to the Mac. I'm looking forward to seeing how touch capability could enhance the Mac experience going forward.

#2: All-new Apple TV 4K

Apple TV hardware has never gone this long between updates. Apple's current latest model is the third-generation Apple TV 4K, released in 2022.

Rumour has it that we'll finally see a new Apple TV 4K in October, with the spotlight on a powerful A19 or A19 Pro chip, along with support for Siri AI features.

Apple raised prices on most of its products this summer, and the Apple TV was no exception. That means this Apple TV 4K, already four years old, now sells for $199 — far higher than its original launch price of $129. I really hope the new Apple TV doesn't cost even more.

#3: The "HomePad"

Rumours about a HomePod with a screen have been around almost as long as the HomePod itself. But such talk began intensifying in 2024, when Mark Gurman published an in-depth report about a product commonly referred to as the "HomePad".

Billy Coker's comment received the most likes

Honestly, I'm really tired of hearing about Apple TV articles until the product actually launches. It's always "coming soon", "coming soon" — but it never actually arrives.

The HomePad is a smart display with a built-in speaker, reportedly set to lead Apple's renewed push into the smart home market. It will run a new operating system with an interface that blends elements of iOS, tvOS and watchOS, including a StandBy-like mode.

Siri AI is expected to be at the core of this product, and it will also come with a camera, customisable widgets, and built-in Apple apps such as Photos, Notes, Music and Calendar.

Which upcoming Apple product are you most looking forward to, in October or beyond? Let us know in the comments.
